## Scratch-table CPU recovery

The current module owns12 complete bodies:571 instructions/1515 original
bytes. The seven additional entries are38DD0C (context constructor),38DD26
(release),38DD54 (table setup/publication),38DE07 (page append),38DE59 (byte
copy),38E668 (address/contiguity request) and38E6DF (page cursor). All346
previous instruction lines remain unchanged. Existing world dispatch admits
these complete entries through the same module; external owners are required.

Produce a fresh original fixture after producing the upload fixture below:

```sh
python3 tools/tag_match_memory_budget.py --output-root NEW_GUARD --timeout 90 -- \
  /tmp/halo2-fov-reference-env/bin/python tools/oracle_sound_gp_scratch_tu15.py \
  --upload-fixtures ABSOLUTE_UPLOAD_FIXTURES --output NEW_ORIGINAL
```

The oracle authenticates the owned executable and adds31 unchanged-original
cases to the existing30. Cases cover all three constructor modes, empty/live
release branches, zero/unaligned/tail/4097-byte copies, zero/multiple descriptor
appends, GP/EP table branches, zero/nonzero prefixes, page cursors and actual
kernel import boundaries. They execute150 instruction addresses. The context,
descriptor state and resource addresses are declared inputs, not recovered
factory outputs. MMIO is an explicitly write-only output sink; any device read
fails. Kernel boundaries stop before execution without a return or ready flag.

Copy the fresh output to the previously absent ignored directory
`tests/fixtures/sound_gp_scratch_tu15`, build `campaign_dsp_image_tu15_tests`
serially within1GiB/zero swap, and run `original_sound_gp_scratch_tu15` through
the60/64MiB/zero-swap guard. The existing reader compares complete retained
banks, GP/XMM, defined flags and every ordered store with/without an observer.
Unused table/data bytes are retained too, so a wrong stride or trailing copy
cannot pass by shrinking the observed footprint.

Original v419, Clang/current-root CMake v422/v423 and frozen GCC v425/v426
pass122 native comparisons,189729 ordered stores and32 external stops across
all61 cases. The older production module fails on the first new entry (v420).
Private descriptor-stride and trailing-copy errors fail retained table/data
bytes (v427/v428). Initial v418 failed because Unicorn required a mapped fetch
address before the stop hook could observe a kernel import. v419 maps only
that stop boundary; no imported instruction executes or produces a result.

Fresh source regeneration v424 reproduces all eleven selected modules at the
current shared-checkout state:179 unique complete bodies/17145 instructions/
62288 original bytes. The new native pool composition independently verifies
the189 data-SGE writes up to the real38DF31 MMIO boundary; see
`sound_gp_pool_tu15.md`. Full prefix/native resource factory, MMIO publication,
translation after the kernel request, processor/device/clock composition and
final audiovisual/installed acceptance remain open. Recovery of complete CPU
bodies does not establish full cutscene-engine parity.

## Upload/allocation recovery and its current execution boundary

The earlier v379 module added complete original388309 (124 instructions)
and38DE81 (80 instructions). Its then-five whole bodies total346 instructions/962
original bytes. The original decoder, descriptor relocation, allocation/free
calls, SGE publication, request3 store and GP polling loop remain in their
real callers. Existing native world dispatch recognizes these entries. Until
the actual GP scratch/DMA request owner is connected, the world stops before
38846E's publication rather than entering a wait with no consuming processor.
The CPU module itself supplies no acknowledgement, allocation success or ready
flag. This is additional source recovery, not a completed native upload path.

Generate a fresh decoder fixture with the command below, then run the upload
oracle under the same mandatory memory guard:

```bash
python3 tools/tag_match_memory_budget.py \
  --output-root analysis/gp-upload-original-NEW-guard --timeout 90 -- \
  /tmp/halo2-fov-reference-env/bin/python tools/oracle_sound_gp_upload_tu15.py \
  --decoder-fixtures analysis/dsp-decoder-original-NEW \
  --output analysis/gp-upload-original-NEW
```

The oracle authenticates the original executable and raw DSPImage section,
copies the independent decoder cases, and executes12 additional caller cases.
Contexts are explicitly declared mathematical/resource inputs, not fabricated
original constructor results. Five cases retain existing storage, two reject
requests beyond reservation, three stop at the actual allocation call38796C,
and two stop at descriptor allocation/free387A32/387A9A. No callee return,
hardware field or GP clear is supplied. They exercise68 new caller instruction
addresses. Later descriptor relocation and GP acknowledgement still require
composed original/native tests.

Copy the complete fresh output into the previously absent ignored directory

## Decoder and original live-upload observations

Use a fresh directory and the required memory guard:

```bash
python3 tools/tag_match_memory_budget.py \
  --output-root analysis/dsp-decoder-original-NEW-guard --timeout 90 -- \
  /tmp/halo2-fov-reference-env/bin/python tools/oracle_sound_dsp_image_tu15.py \
  --output analysis/dsp-decoder-original-NEW
```

The oracle authenticates the owned TU1.5 executable and executes its original
38DF59, 38DFD2 and 38DFFF instructions unchanged. The declared mutable input
buffer contains the actual DSPImage section. The 18 cases cover initialization,
the embedded seed table, all 15 effect payloads, and a stop immediately after
the original `IMUL BL` instruction. No source callee return is supplied.

Copy the complete previously absent output directory to the ignored
`tests/fixtures/sound_dsp_image_tu15` to enable
`original_campaign_sound_dsp_image_tu15`. Preserve prior evidence. The native
reader compares every retained byte, GP/XMM state, defined flags and the ordered
store digest. Each digest item encodes three little-endian u32 words (original
instruction, address, extent), then the original before and written bytes.
The intermediate multiply boundary compares only architecturally defined CF/OF.

The previous 32-bit lowering fails the intermediate GP comparison, although its
eventual decoded bytes match. This is a CPU decoder test. DSP program execution,
DMA, hardware address relocation, sound admission and audible parity remain
outside its scope.

The uploaded program can also be checked against an unchanged original cold
boot. Run `tools/capture_live_sound_dsp_tu15.py` through GDB's Python against an
isolated, paused xemu with hardware breakpoints, a new
`H2_DSP_CAPTURE_OUTPUT`, and `H2_DSP_DECODED_REFERENCE` pointing to this fixture
directory. Enable `audio.use_dsp` in that private emulator configuration to
finish each DSP frame before capture. The observer never writes guest code,
memory, registers, service returns or ready flags. It retains live program,
parameter, mix and delay memory and confirms stable repeated readback.

Then run the audit under the same required memory guard:

```bash
python3 tools/tag_match_memory_budget.py \
  --output-root analysis/dsp-upload-NEW-guard --timeout 60 -- \
  python3 tools/audit_uploaded_sound_dsp_tu15.py \
  --capture analysis/ORIGINAL-CAPTURE/capture \
  --decoded tests/fixtures/sound_dsp_image_tu15 \
  --native /absolute/path/to/campaign_audio_tu15_tests \
  --output analysis/dsp-upload-NEW
```

The native argument is optional and selects the decoder fixture reader. The
upload audit checks all15 payloads/14204 bytes plus the original unencrypted
final return word, for14208 exact program bytes. It locates execution from the
original GP control program, because effect descriptor pointers skip each
two-word R5 prologue. A deliberate one-bit uploaded-code change fails with the
exact GP byte address. This adds an original live-upload reference to decoder
recovery; it still does not establish native DSP execution, timing, final mix,
whole-engine coverage or physical Xbox audio parity.

The current observer additionally retains the actual GP scratch image through
GPSADDR/GPSMAXSGE and the physical scatter/gather table. It checks the scratch
header against GP X memory, the control program against both scratch and the
original executable, and every effect-delay interval against its CPU pointer.
An effect-allocation relocation bias alone does not describe the control/image
scratch prefix. The audit rejects that incomplete mapping. The control program
adds1476 authenticated bytes, for15684 complete loaded GP program bytes.
For older captures, `--observer` can select their retained observer source;
observer hashes are never silently ignored.
